clauses.mechanism: spent_on_issue: self-executing amendments of the Manual for Courts-Martial effective 30 days after signing
clauses.reason: Sec. 1 amends Parts III and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial "as described in the Annex"; that self-executing amendment took effect with the order under Sec. 2, 30 days after the December 13, 2011 signing, on January 12, 2012, and left nothing further for the order to command. The amended text lives on in the Manual.

clauses.mechanism: spent_on_issue: self-executing amendments of the Manual for Courts-Martial effective 30 days after signing
clauses.reason: Sec. 2 sets the effective date of the amendments ("These amendments shall take effect 30 days from the date of this" order), which is January 12, 2012; the provision was exhausted when that date arrived.

clauses.mechanism: spent_on_issue: self-executing amendments of the Manual for Courts-Martial effective 30 days after signing
clauses.reason: Sec. 2(a) is a rule of construction that the amendments do not make punishable any act done or omitted before the effective date of January 12, 2012 that was not punishable when done; it only limits how the Sec. 1 amendments apply to past conduct and was fixed as of the effective date, so it is recorded as ended on that date with its protective effect carried under savings.

clauses.mechanism: spent_on_issue: self-executing amendments of the Manual for Courts-Martial effective 30 days after signing
clauses.reason: Sec. 2(b) is a rule of construction preserving proceedings begun before the effective date of January 12, 2012; it covers only actions begun before that date, a closed class, and is recorded as ended on that date with the preserved proceedings carried under savings.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13593 (December 13, 2011; 76 FR 78451) amends Parts III and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States (prescribed by Executive Order 12473, as amended) as described in an Annex, and Sec. 2 provides that the amendments take effect 30 days from the date of the order, that is January 12, 2012. Its operative acts are self-executing amendments of the Manual: the order contains no continuing duty, reporting requirement or standing command, and Sec. 2(a) and (b) are rules of construction that protect conduct and proceedings begun before the effective date. The amended text continues as text of the Manual, which is a separate instrument, so the order's own commands were spent on its effective date, January 12, 2012. Searches of held texts for the number 13593 found only the order's own Federal Register text and later Federal Register documents that implement, cite or annotate it (2011-32486, 2012-25852, 2013-07804, 2016-06403, 2016-21874); none revokes, supersedes or amends it, and the Federal Register catalog note is empty, which does not by itself show current effect.

The later Federal Register documents that cite it (listed in the rationale) recite or implement the amendments; none ends the order, and the bounded machine searches report no ending instrument.","independent_command_check":"Sec. 2(a) and 2(b) are not independent commands: they limit how the Sec. 1 amendments apply to acts and proceedings before the effective date. The Annex's inserted Manual text is amendment content, not a command of the order.","savings_check":"Surviving effects are the amended Manual text and the pre-effective-date proceedings preserved by Sec. 2(b); both are recorded under savings as transferred or accrued.","scope_check":"The order has two substantive provisions: Sec. 1 (the amendments of Parts III and IV) and Sec. 2 with its two rules of construction. All four scopes ended together on the effective date; no partial revocation was located."}

savings.reason: The amendments continue as text of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States (prescribed by Executive Order 12473, as amended), which is a separate instrument; the surviving text is not a command of Executive Order 13593. Sec. 2(b) of the order also preserves proceedings begun before the effective date, which may proceed in the same manner and with the same effect as if the amendments had not been prescribed; that accrued protection attaches to those pre-effective-date matters.
